subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: Who served as the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission of India under Chairman Jawaharlal Nehru in 1950?
options: A) Gulzarilal Nanda
B) V.T. Krishnamachari
C) C.D. Deshmukh
D) K.C. Neogy
questions.explanation: Gulzarilal Nanda was appointed as the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission in March 1950, overseeing its early operational planning.

questions.question: Who was appointed by the Government of India as the Agent-General in Hyderabad to negotiate with the Nizam during the tense Standstill Agreement of 1947-1948?
options: A) V.P. Menon
B) K.M. Munshi
C) N.V. Gadgil
D) H.M. Patel
questions.explanation: K.M. Munshi served as India's Agent-General in Hyderabad, monitoring the deteriorating internal security situation and the violent atrocities committed by the Razakars.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Which Austrian diplomat and statesman served as the fourth Secretary-General of the United Nations from 1972 to 1981?
options: A) U Thant
B) Javier Perez de Cuellar
C) Kurt Waldheim
D) Boutros Boutros-Ghali
questions.explanation: Kurt Waldheim of Austria served two five-year terms as UN Secretary-General from 1972 to 1981 before later becoming President of Austria.

questions.question: What core ideological distinction separated the Swatantra Party formed in 1959 from the Indian National Congress?
options: A) The Swatantra Party demanded the complete nationalisation of all foreign private banks and heavy industries
B) The Swatantra Party advocated an immediate armed communist peasant revolution modeled on the Soviet Union
C) The Swatantra Party demanded the restoration of the British colonial governor-generalship over Indian states
D) The Swatantra Party stood for free enterprise, minimal state intervention, and individual liberty, vigorously opposing state-controlled licensing and cooperatives
questions.explanation: Founded by C. Rajagopalachari, Minoo Masani, and N.G. Ranga, the Swatantra Party advocated laissez-faire capitalism, tax reductions, and the abolition of the 'License-Permit-Quota Raj'.

questions.question: Which United Nations mediator submitted the famous 'Dixon Plan' in September 1950 proposing regional plebiscites in Jammu and Kashmir, which was rejected by both India and Pakistan?
options: A) Sir Owen Dixon
B) General A.G.L. McNaughton
C) Dr. Frank Graham
D) Gunnar Jarring
questions.explanation: Australian jurist Sir Owen Dixon proposed allocating Ladakh to India, northern areas and Azad Kashmir to Pakistan, and holding a plebiscite limited to the Kashmir Valley, which failed to secure agreement.

questions.question: What was the main argument presented by Choudhary Charan Singh in his seminal 1978 work 'India's Economic Policy: The Gandhian Blueprint' regarding national planning?
options: A) That India must instantly dismantle all rural cottage handlooms and import synthetic textiles exclusively from the United States
B) That disproportionate planning allocations to capital-intensive heavy industries created rural unemployment and that agriculture must be the center of Indian planning
C) That all agricultural land should be transferred to large corporate joint ventures listed on the stock exchange
D) That the Planning Commission should be replaced with a military supreme command
questions.explanation: Charan Singh argued that Nehruvian heavy industrialisation drained resources from the agrarian sector, created urban-rural inequalities, and demanded that agriculture and cottage industries receive top priority.

questions.question: What was the core conclusion of the classified Henderson Brooks-Bhagat Report commissioned by the Indian Army in 1963?
options: A) It concluded that the Indian armed forces had achieved all of their tactical and territorial objectives along the Himalayan frontier
B) It recommended the complete abolition of the Indian Army in favor of a decentralized state militia
C) It revealed severe systemic failures in military intelligence, higher command leadership, flawed political assumptions, and inadequate equipment during the 1962 Sino-Indian War
D) It established that China had used chemical weapons against Indian border posts in Ladakh
questions.explanation: The Henderson Brooks-Bhagat operational review exposed serious deficiencies in political-military decision-making, the unrealistic Forward Policy, poor logistic planning, and intelligence failures in 1962.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In the fourth General Election of 1967, which state government was formed by the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) under Chief Minister C.N. Annadurai, creating a landmark in Indian regional politics?
options: A) Andhra Pradesh
B) Kerala
C) Mysore State
D) Madras State (later renamed Tamil Nadu)
questions.explanation: The DMK won an absolute majority in Madras State in 1967, forming the first non-Congress single-party majority state government in post-independence India and renaming the state Tamil Nadu in 1969.

questions.question: What was the primary holding of the Supreme Court in the historic Raj Narain v. Indira Gandhi (1975) appeal concerning the 39th Constitutional Amendment?
options: A) Striking down Article 329A(4) which sought to validate Indira Gandhi's election and bar judicial review, ruling that free and fair elections and judicial review are basic features of the Constitution
B) Declaring that the Prime Minister of India possesses absolute immunity from any civil or criminal proceeding in any court
C) Abolishing the Representation of the People Act, 1951, as unconstitutional and ultra vires
D) Directing that all future general elections must be conducted by the International Court of Justice
questions.explanation: In Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975), the Supreme Court struck down clause (4) of Article 329A inserted by the 39th Amendment, applying the basic structure doctrine to invalidate an amendment for the first time.

questions.question: Which accord signed in February 1993 between the Government of India, the Government of Assam, and the All Bodo Students Union (ABSU) created an autonomous council within Assam?
options: A) Karbi Anglong Accord
B) Bodo Accord (creating the Bodoland Autonomous Council)
C) Dimasa Territorial Accord
D) Cachar Hills Concordat
questions.explanation: The 1993 Bodo Accord established the Bodoland Autonomous Council (BAC) to provide administrative autonomy to the Bodo tribal areas within Assam, following intense student agitation.

questions.question: In 1998, which visionary defense analyst and former director of the Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses (IDSA) chaired the committee that drafted India's Draft Nuclear Doctrine?
options: A) Raja Ramanna
B) J.N. Dixit
C) K. Subrahmanyam
D) Brajesh Mishra
questions.explanation: K. Subrahmanyam chaired the National Security Advisory Board (NSAB) which formulated the Draft Nuclear Doctrine in August 1999, proposing 'Credible Minimum Deterrence' and 'No First Use'.

questions.question: What major political development occurred in February 1999 when Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee took the inaugural 'Sada-e-Sarhad' bus journey from Delhi to Lahore?
options: A) Signing a tripartite defense treaty with Pakistan and China establishing a demilitarized border
B) Announcing the immediate political reunification of India and Pakistan under a joint parliament
C) Ceding the Siachen Glacier to the United Nations Military Observer Group
D) Signing the historic Lahore Declaration with Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif to promote bilateral peace and nuclear risk reduction
questions.explanation: Vajpayee traveled to Lahore on the inaugural bus service on 19 February 1999 and signed the Lahore Declaration with Nawaz Sharif, inaugurating a historic peace initiative before it was derailed by Kargil.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: In the Caucasus republic of Georgia, which pro-Western popular movement in November 2003 ousted President Eduard Shevardnadze and brought Mikheil Saakashvili to power?
options: A) Rose Revolution
B) Orange Revolution
C) Tulip Revolution
D) Velvet Revolution
questions.explanation: The Rose Revolution of November 2003 was a non-violent pro-democracy popular uprising in Georgia following disputed parliamentary elections, ushering in reformist Mikheil Saakashvili.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Under the 1997 Kyoto Protocol, which international carbon offset mechanism enabled developed countries to trade emissions reduction units with one another?
options: A) Global Green Currency Exchange
B) International Emissions Trading (IET)
C) Universal Carbon Tariff Protocol
D) Sustainable Hydrocarbon Swap
questions.explanation: Article 17 of the Kyoto Protocol established International Emissions Trading, allowing Annex B countries with unused permitted emissions to sell excess units to countries over their targets.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: What was the landmark foreign policy doctrine enunciated by Prime Minister I.K. Gujral in 1996 governing India's relations with its immediate South Asian neighbors?
options: A) Indira Doctrine (asserting India's sole military hegemony across the Indian Ocean)
B) Nehruvian Realpolitik (maintaining armed buffer zones along all land borders)
C) Gujral Doctrine (unilateral non-reciprocal concessions to smaller neighbors based on goodwill and mutual trust)
D) Vajpayee Security Protocol (demanding equal reciprocal concessions on all bilateral disputes)
questions.explanation: The Gujral Doctrine asserted that India, as the largest South Asian state, should not ask for reciprocity from smaller neighbors like Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan, and Sri Lanka, but give whatever it can in good faith.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Which international judicial tribunal based in The Hague was established in 2002 under the Rome Statute to prosecute individuals for genocide, crimes against humanity, and war crimes?
options: A) International Court of Justice (ICJ)
B) Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA)
C) Nuremberg Tribunal
D) International Criminal Court (ICC)
questions.explanation: The International Criminal Court (ICC), operating independently of the UN in The Hague, investigates and prosecutes individuals for the gravest international crimes (genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity).

questions.question: What is the primary rationale behind the global humanitarian campaign that led to the 1997 Ottawa Treaty (Mine Ban Treaty)?
options: A) To prohibit the use, stockpiling, production, and transfer of anti-personnel landmines because of their indiscriminate and lingering maiming of civilian populations
B) To mandate the global decommissioning of all conventional maritime naval submarines
C) To force all national armies to surrender their inventory of assault rifles to the United Nations
D) To ban the manufacture of armed drones and military communication satellites
questions.explanation: The Ottawa Convention (1997) banned anti-personnel landmines due to their devastating, indiscriminate civilian casualties and long-term economic destruction of agricultural lands.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: Which international declaration adopted in 1972 at the United Nations Conference on the Human Environment in Stockholm served as the foundational manifesto of modern international environmental law?
options: A) Rio Declaration
B) Stockholm Declaration
C) Kyoto Declaration
D) Brundtland Charter
questions.explanation: The 1972 Stockholm Declaration, containing 26 principles, marked the first major global summit on environmental protection and inspired the creation of national environmental ministries worldwide.

questions.question: Which four senior Communist Party leaders traveled clandestinely to Moscow in 1951 to consult with Joseph Stalin, resulting in the Tactical Line document that led the CPI to abandon armed revolution for parliamentary elections?
options: A) P.C. Joshi, B.T. Ranadive, E.M.S. Namboodiripad, and A.K. Gopalan
B) Muzaffar Ahmad, S.V. Ghate, S.S. Mirajkar, and Bankim Mukherjee
C) Ajoy Ghosh, S.A. Dange, C. Rajeswara Rao, and M. Basavapunnaiah
D) Harkishan Singh Surjeet, Jyoti Basu, Biman Bose, and Somnath Chatterjee
questions.explanation: In early 1951, a four-member delegation (Ajoy Ghosh, S.A. Dange, C. Rajeswara Rao, and M. Basavapunnaiah) met Stalin in Moscow; the resulting Tactical Line directed the party to participate in the 1951-52 general elections.

questions.question: Under the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, enacted alongside the States Reorganisation Act, what fundamental structural change was made to the categorization of Indian constituent states?
options: A) Dividing India into four autonomous regional confederations governed by elected military governors
B) Eliminating all state legislative assemblies in favor of direct central administration from New Delhi
C) Creating an independent sovereign republic for each of the major 22 scheduled languages
D) Abolishing the four-fold classification into Part A, Part B, Part C, and Part D states, replacing them with 14 States and 6 Union Territories
questions.explanation: The 7th Amendment abolished the colonial Part A, B, C, D classification and the institution of Rajpramukh, establishing a uniform constitutional status for 14 States and 6 Union Territories.

questions.question: Which foreign funding mechanism provided crucial financial and commodity support (gift of butter oil and skimmed milk powder) to launch Phase I of India's 'Operation Flood' in 1970?
options: A) The European Economic Community (EEC) through the World Food Programme (WFP)
B) The United States Export-Import Bank under the Marshall Aid Protocol
C) The Soviet Gosplan Foreign Assistance Directorate in Moscow
D) The International Monetary Fund's Structural Adjustment Facility
questions.explanation: Under Operation Flood Phase I, food aid donated by the European Economic Community via the World Food Programme was monetized by the National Dairy Development Board to fund dairy cooperatives.

questions.question: What was the significance of United Nations Security Council Resolution 211 passed on 20 September 1965 during the Indo-Pakistani War?
options: A) It ordered the immediate military dismemberment of Pakistan into two sovereign independent republics
B) It demanded that an immediate unconditional ceasefire take effect on 22 September and that both armed forces withdraw to positions held prior to 5 August 1965
C) It mandated that the entire territory of Jammu and Kashmir be placed under permanent NATO administration
D) It authorized the deployment of a 100,000-strong multinational combat invasion force in the Punjab plains
questions.explanation: UNSC Resolution 211 demanded a ceasefire by 22 September 1965 and troop withdrawals to the status quo ante bellum as of 5 August 1965, laying the foundation for the Tashkent Conference.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which regional leader in Uttar Pradesh formed the Bharatiya Kranti Dal (BKD) after defecting from C.B. Gupta's Congress ministry in April 1967, becoming the first non-Congress Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh?
options: A) Ram Manohar Lohia
B) Chandra Shekhar
C) Choudhary Charan Singh
D) Hemvati Nandan Bahuguna
questions.explanation: Charan Singh walked out of the Congress with 16 MLAs on 1 April 1967, formed the Bharatiya Kranti Dal (BKD), and took oath as Chief Minister heading the SVD coalition government in UP.

questions.question: In the landmark Minerva Mills judgment of 1980, which specific sub-clause of Article 31C inserted by the 42nd Amendment—giving primacy to all Directive Principles over Fundamental Rights—was struck down by the Supreme Court?
options: A) Article 31C as originally inserted by the 25th Amendment Act, 1971
B) Article 368 clause (1) defining the constituent amending power of Parliament
C) Article 13 clause (4) exempting constitutional amendments from judicial scrutiny
D) Article 31C as amended by Section 4 of the 42nd Amendment Act
questions.explanation: In Minerva Mills, CJI Y.V. Chandrachud struck down Section 4 of the 42nd Amendment, holding that to destroy Fundamental Rights to achieve Directive Principles upends the harmony that is a basic structure of the Constitution.

questions.question: Which judicial commission was appointed under the Commissions of Inquiry Act in November 1984 to investigate the organized anti-Sikh violence in Delhi, but was widely criticized for clearing political leaders before being superseded by the Nanavati Commission in 2000?
options: A) Justice Ranganath Misra Commission
B) Justice Sarkaria Commission
C) Justice Shah Commission
D) Justice Liberhan Commission
questions.explanation: The Ranganath Misra Commission submitted its report in 1986, which faced sharp public criticism for failing to indict senior Congress leaders; the Justice G.T. Nanavati Commission was appointed in 2000 to conduct a thorough inquiry.

questions.question: In the coalition history of India, which unique power-sharing arrangement was devised in Uttar Pradesh in 1997 between the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Bahujan Samaj Party?
options: A) A dual-governor system where two state governors held veto power over the cabinet
B) A rotational Chief Minister formula under which Mayawati (BSP) and Kalyan Singh (BJP) would each govern for six months
C) An alternating legislative session formula where parties chaired the assembly in alternate months
D) A permanent coalition where the BSP held all finance portfolios and the BJP held all police posts
questions.explanation: The innovative 'six-month rotational Chief Minister' pact collapsed in October 1997 shortly after Mayawati transferred power to Kalyan Singh, leading to a bitter political falling out.

questions.question: Under the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act passed by the Indian Parliament in 2003, what statutory mandate was laid down for macroeconomic management?
options: A) Mandating that all foreign direct investment in retail trade must be approved by state legislatures
B) Prohibiting commercial banks from lending credit to agricultural and rural cooperative societies
C) Institutionalizing financial discipline, reducing the fiscal deficit to 3% of GDP, and eliminating the revenue deficit over a target timeframe
D) Fixing the exchange rate of the Indian rupee permanently against the International Monetary Fund's SDR
questions.explanation: Enacted in 2003 under the Vajpayee government, the FRBM Act established statutory targets to enforce fiscal discipline, curb runaway government debt, and eliminate the structural revenue deficit.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which former Soviet republic witnessed the 'Tulip Revolution' in March 2005, ousting President Askar Akayev following allegations of parliamentary election rigging?
options: A) Tajikistan
B) Uzbekistan
C) Turkmenistan
D) Kyrgyzstan
questions.explanation: The Tulip Revolution (Pink or Silk Revolution) took place in Kyrgyzstan in March 2005, forcing President Askar Akayev to flee to Russia following mass street demonstrations against corruption.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: What is the primary function of the 'European Central Bank' (ECB) established in Frankfurt, Germany, in 1998?
options: A) Conducting monetary policy for the eurozone, maintaining price stability (inflation control), and managing foreign reserve assets
B) Collecting national income taxes from citizens across all 27 European Union member states
C) Directly financing the military defense budgets of individual NATO member states in Europe
D) Managing commercial agricultural farms in southern Europe under the Common Fisheries Policy
questions.explanation: The ECB, operational since 1 June 1998 in Frankfurt, is the supranational monetary authority for the eurozone, tasked with maintaining price stability and managing the euro currency.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: In Sri Lanka's ethnic conflict, which Norwegian diplomat served as the chief peace facilitator between the Sri Lankan Government and the LTTE, negotiating the 2002 Ceasefire Agreement (CFA)?
options: A) Martti Ahtisaari
B) Erik Solheim
C) Kofi Annan
D) Thorvald Stoltenberg
questions.explanation: Erik Solheim of Norway served as the principal international mediator from 2000 to 2006, brokering the landmark February 2002 Ceasefire Agreement between Colombo and the LTTE.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Under the UN Charter, what unique constitutional procedure is required under Article 108 to pass a formal amendment to the Charter of the United Nations?
options: A) A simple majority of the General Assembly with no ratification needed by any national parliament
B) Approval by the International Court of Justice followed by an executive order of the Secretary-General
C) Adoption by a two-thirds vote of the General Assembly and ratification by two-thirds of member states, including all five permanent members of the Security Council
D) Unanimous vote by all 193 member states assembled at an extraordinary plenary session in Geneva
questions.explanation: Article 108 requires a two-thirds vote in the UNGA and ratification by two-thirds of members, specifically including the ratifications of all P5 states (US, Russia, China, UK, France), giving each P5 member a veto over Charter amendments.

questions.question: Which international convention adopted in 2005 under UN auspices was the first to address the threat of non-state terrorist actors acquiring nuclear weapons or radioactive dispersal devices?
options: A) Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW)
B) Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (START I)
C) Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material (CPPNM)
D) International Convention for the Suppression of Acts of Nuclear Terrorism (ICSANT)
questions.explanation: ICSANT was adopted by the UN General Assembly in April 2005, criminalizing the possession, use, or threat of nuclear materials and radiological dirty bombs by terrorist individuals or non-state groups.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: In international environmental law, what is the core meaning of the 'Precautionary Principle' enshrined in Principle 15 of the 1992 Rio Declaration?
options: A) Where there are threats of serious or irreversible damage, lack of full scientific certainty shall not be used as a reason for postponing cost-effective environmental measures
B) Governments must completely suspend all industrial production whenever any ecological protest occurs
C) Developing countries must pay financial indemnity bonds to multinational corporations before enacting pollution laws
D) All international environmental treaties must be drafted and approved exclusively by nuclear physicists
questions.explanation: Principle 15 states that lack of full scientific certainty cannot justify delaying protective action when there is a risk of serious or irreversible ecological harm.

questions.question: Which theoretical concept formulated by political economist Susan Strange in 'The Retreat of the State' (1996) captures the structural change in state sovereignty under globalized finance?
options: A) Sovereign states have absorbed all private multinational corporations into socialist state ministries
B) Structural power in the global economy has shifted from national territorial states to multinational corporations and impersonal global financial markets
C) Globalisation has restored the absolute territorial sovereignty of 17th-century Westphalian monarchies
D) National boundaries have been physically fortified with automated surveillance robots
questions.explanation: Susan Strange argued that the globalization of finance, technology, and production has eroded national state autonomy, transferring real structural decision-making power to market forces and transnational firms.

questions.question: Which pioneering Indian sociologist and election analyst described the first three general elections as the foundation of the 'Congress System', defining it as a system of one-party dominance with competitive internal consensus?
options: A) M.N. Srinivas
B) Andre Beteille
C) Rajni Kothari
D) G.S. Ghurye
questions.explanation: Rajni Kothari published his seminal article 'The Congress System in India' in 1964 in Asian Survey, conceptualizing Congress dominance as a democratic consensus-building umbrella system.

questions.question: Under which historic agreement signed in July 1949 was the territorial boundary between India and Pakistan demarcated across the rugged glacier terrain of Jammu and Kashmir up to point NJ9842?
options: A) Tashkent Protocol of 1966
B) Simla Agreement of 1972
C) Lahore Concordat of 1999
D) Karachi Ceasefire Agreement of 1949
questions.explanation: The Karachi Agreement of 27 July 1949, supervised by the UN Commission for India and Pakistan (UNCIP), established the ceasefire line ending the 1947-48 war, concluding at map coordinate NJ9842.

questions.question: What was the administrative controversy associated with the creation of the Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) in January 1973 under Steel Minister Mohan Kumaramangalam?
options: A) It created a massive holding company model intended to coordinate both public and private steel enterprises, vesting enormous centralized bureaucratic control in the Steel Ministry
B) It completely transferred all Indian iron ore mines to multinational mining firms from Wall Street
C) It prohibited any Indian engineer from working in heavy manufacturing plants across Bihar and Bengal
D) It required all steel manufactured in India to be exported exclusively to Eastern European nations
questions.explanation: Mohan Kumaramangalam established SAIL as an overarching holding company to plan, promote, and organize the growth of the steel industry, representing the zenith of state-led industrial planning under Indira Gandhi.

questions.question: Which clause of the 1972 Shimla Agreement between Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto became India's foundational diplomatic anchor resisting third-party mediation in the Kashmir dispute?
options: A) Clause 3(iv) authorizing the United Nations Security Council to arbitrate all border demarcations
B) Clause 1(ii) committing both nations to settle their differences by peaceful means through bilateral negotiations
C) Clause 5(i) requiring both nations to maintain equal defense spending registered with the World Bank
D) Clause 6(ii) establishing a permanent joint Indo-Pakistani legislative parliament in Lahore
questions.explanation: Clause 1(ii) of the Shimla Agreement established the principle of bilateralism, committing both states to resolve disputes peacefully through direct bilateral talks, ruling out third-party international mediation.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which of the following describes the key provision of the 25th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1971, enacted by Indira Gandhi's government following the bank nationalization cases?
options: A) Abolishing the Supreme Court of India's jurisdiction over civil property disputes entirely
B) Mandating that all private corporate assets must be transferred to the Prime Minister's Relief Fund
C) Replacing the word 'compensation' in Article 31(2) with 'amount', thereby eliminating judicial review over the adequacy of compensation paid for acquired property
D) Prohibiting any Indian citizen from holding bank deposits exceeding 1,000 rupees
questions.explanation: The 25th Amendment substituted 'amount' for 'compensation' in Article 31(2) to overcome the Supreme Court's R.C. Cooper ruling requiring market-value compensation for nationalized commercial banks.

questions.question: In which state did the student-led agitation in 1974 against food shortages, inflation, and government corruption culminate in Jayaprakash Narayan issuing his historic call for 'Total Revolution'?
options: A) Gujarat
B) Uttar Pradesh
C) West Bengal
D) Bihar
questions.explanation: In March 1974, students in Bihar formed the Chatra Sangharsh Samiti to protest corruption, unemployment, and food price rises, inviting JP to lead them on the condition that the agitation remain strictly non-violent.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution, inserted by the 37th Amendment in 1975, provided for the creation of a Legislative Assembly and Council of Ministers for the Union Territory of Arunachal Pradesh prior to its statehood in 1987?
options: A) Article 239A
B) Article 371A
C) Article 371H
D) Article 240
questions.explanation: The 37th Amendment Act, 1975, amended Article 239A and Article 240 to create a legislature and council of ministers for Arunachal Pradesh, preparing the frontier territory for full statehood in 1987.

questions.question: Which influential thesis on Indian political parties, propounded by political scientist Paul Brass, conceptualized the political consolidation of rich peasants and OBCs in northern India under Charan Singh?
options: A) The Theory of Feudal Restorationism
B) The Coalition of Middle Peasants (Jat-Yadav-Kurmi-Koeri agrarian alliance)
C) The Industrial Bourgeoisie Hegemony Model
D) The Monolithic Caste Polarization Thesis
questions.explanation: Paul Brass documented how Choudhary Charan Singh organized middle peasant castes (Jats, Yadavs, Kurmis, Koeris) against urban upper-caste hegemony, creating the foundational base for modern north Indian regional parties.

questions.question: In the landmark S.R. Bommai case (1994), what specific operational test did the Supreme Court lay down for evaluating whether a state Council of Ministers enjoys legislative majority, strictly limiting the subjective discretion of the State Governor?
options: A) A secret physical parade of legislators held inside the Governor's official residence
B) A public signature petition submitted by party whips to the Election Commission of India
C) The Floor Test on the floor of the State Legislative Assembly is the only constitutionally valid test of majority
D) A confidential intelligence report prepared by the state director general of police
questions.explanation: In Bommai (1994), the Supreme Court ruled that the floor of the House is the only forum to test the majority of a ministry, barring Governors from dismissing governments based on private assessments.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which autonomous republic within the Russian Federation adopted a constitution in 1992 declaring itself a sovereign state in association with Russia, but resolved its status peacefully through a bilateral power-sharing treaty with Moscow in 1994?
options: A) Chechnya
B) Dagestan
C) North Ossetia
D) Tatarstan
questions.explanation: Under President Mintimer Shaimiev, Tatarstan avoided the violent fate of Chechnya by negotiating a historic bilateral power-sharing treaty with Boris Yeltsin's government in February 1994 granting wide autonomy.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Under the European Union's 'Common Agricultural Policy' (CAP) established in 1962, what was the primary economic mechanism used to guarantee farmers' incomes and food security?
options: A) Direct price supports, import tariffs on external agricultural produce, and export subsidies to clear internal surpluses
B) The mandatory collectivization of all farmland into state-owned industrial agro-complexes
C) The prohibition of any private ownership of dairy cattle across France and Germany
D) A permanent ban on the cultivation of wheat and barley in western European nations
questions.explanation: The CAP historically utilized internal price supports, external tariffs, and export restitutions to achieve European food self-sufficiency, before transitioning toward direct decoupled farm payments.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: What was the diplomatic crisis in December 1999 that severely tested India's counter-terrorism policy and resulted in the release of three terrorists in exchange for passengers of hijacked Indian Airlines flight IC-814 at Kandahar?
options: A) The Parliament Attack Hostage Standoff
B) The Kandahar Hijacking Crisis
C) The Colombo Diplomatic Enclave Siege
D) The Charsadda Air Piracy Standoff
questions.explanation: Indian Airlines flight IC-814 was hijacked by Jaish-e-Mohammed operatives on 24 December 1999, forcing India to release three jailed militants (including Masood Azhar) in Taliban-controlled Kandahar to save 176 hostages.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Under Chapter VI of the UN Charter, what peaceful methods of dispute settlement are specifically listed under Article 33 for parties to any dispute likely to endanger international peace?
options: A) Unilateral naval blockades, aerial bombardment, targeted assassinations, and cyber warfare
B) Immediate expulsion of all diplomatic personnel and confiscation of sovereign foreign reserves
C) Negotiation, enquiry, mediation, conciliation, arbitration, judicial settlement, and resort to regional agencies or arrangements
D) Mandatory economic sanctions and dissolution of national sovereign parliaments
questions.explanation: Article 33 of Chapter VI obligates states to seek peaceful resolution through negotiation, enquiry, mediation, conciliation, arbitration, judicial settlement, or regional arrangements before resorting to other measures.

questions.question: Which landmark bilateral strategic treaty signed in April 2010 between President Barack Obama and President Dmitry Medvedev in Prague superseded the 1991 START I treaty, capping deployed strategic nuclear warheads at 1,550?
options: A) Strategic Offensive Reductions Treaty (SORT)
B) Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces (INF) Treaty
C) Open Skies Treaty
D) New START Treaty
questions.explanation: The New START Treaty signed in Prague in 2010 capped deployed strategic nuclear warheads at 1,550 and deployed intercontinental delivery vehicles at 700 for each superpower with on-site inspection protocols.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: In international marine conservation, what is the 'BBNJ Agreement' adopted by the United Nations in June 2023 under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)?
options: A) The High Seas Treaty on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction
B) The Global Treaty on the Commercial Privatization of Deep Sea Hydrocarbon Reservoirs
C) The Multilateral Protocol Mandating Military Naval Conscription on High Seas Merchant Fleets
D) The International Convention Partitioning Pacific Ocean Fisheries to G7 Member States
questions.explanation: Adopted in June 2023, the historic BBNJ High Seas Treaty provides a binding legal framework to establish marine protected areas, assess environmental impacts, and share benefits from marine genetic resources in international waters.

questions.question: Which concept coined by French sociologist Pierre Bourdieu describes how neo-liberal globalization portrays free-market deregulation, privatization, and welfare rollbacks not as political choices, but as inevitable laws of economic nature?
options: A) The Cultural Homogenization Inevitability Paradox
B) The Structural Dependency Determinism Axiom
C) The 'TINA' syndrome (There Is No Alternative) and neo-liberal symbolic violence
